summary: H. G. Quaritch Wales worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a bachelor's at Queens' College, Cambridge, and a Ph.D. at SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden, later serving at the Greater India Society and Royal Asiatic Society.
H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and served as a professor at the University of Mysore.
Hae-ju Sunim specializes in Buddhist studies. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as an associate professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University.

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She earned her MA at Peking University under Jin Kemu, also studying under Zhongxin Jiang, and served as director at the University of Freiburg in 2010.

Hajime Kitamura was a linguistics and Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Reitaku University as president, and Toyo Bunko as board chairman.

Hajime Nakamura specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earning his doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo and director of both Toho Gakuin and the Eastern Institute.

Hajime Okayama worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology, studying at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, and under Xianlin Ji in China. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo and as head of Chuo Buddhist College.

Hajime Sakurabe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi at Otani University, where he completed his PhD and taught from 1952, serving as professor from 1971 to 1986.

Philosopher Hajime Tanabe studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, in Germany under Heinrich Rickert and Martin Heidegger, and with Kitaro Nishida. He received a doctorate from Kyoto University, where he taught from 1919 to 1945.
Hakuin Ekaku was a Japanese figure in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Dōkyō Etan and Hakuyūshi, and he taught Suiō Genro.

Hakuju Ui was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo, as well as in Tübingen and Oxford. He taught at Tohoku University and the University of Tokyo, and served as Komazawa University's president.

Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani was a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Daiun Sogaku Harada and several traditional teachers, and he founded the Sanbo Zen organization in 1954.
Hakuyu Hadano specialized in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served on the faculty at Tohoku University, where he was an assistant professor and later professor emeritus.

Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. He studied at Komazawa University and under teachers including Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani and Koryu Osaka, later serving at Zenshuji Soto Mission and founding the Zen Center of Los Angeles.

Halle O'Neal specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler and serves as co-director at the University of Edinburgh.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Banaras Hindu University and a Ph.D. from Edinburgh. He headed the London Buddhist Vihara, held posts at SOAS and the University of Toronto, and was vice president of the Pali Text Society.

Han de Wit works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and under Adriaan de Groot and Chögyam Trungpa, later holding a post at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
Hank Glassman is a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He has served as a faculty member at Haverford College.
Hanna Havnevik specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She served as a professor and later professor emerita at the University of Oslo.

Hanns Oertel was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale, Marburg, and Basel, and held the chair of Indian and Iranian philology at the University of Munich (1925–1935).
